_comment: Per-unit release lanes (docs/adr/1650-per-unit-control-plane-releases.md). Every release binary (Makefile DAEMONS + CLIS) appears here. lane: control-plane = runs only on the control plane and deploys alone through cd-controlplane's unit lane; edge = the gateways, deployed after the control plane by cd-edge-units.yml one host at a time (services name the host role they run on); shared = also runs on compute hosts, so a change waits for the full release; compute = compute hosts only; tool = operator/customer CLI, never restarted. pkg/daemonunitspec/release_units_lane_test.go keeps lanes, services and readiness URLs in lockstep with the daemon registry; scripts/ci/affected_units_test.py keeps the binary set in lockstep with the Makefile.

gates._comment: SLO gate per host (scripts/ci/slo_gate.py --duration/--max-hold). The canary is the first host of a lane: the control plane in the control-plane lane, the designated compute node in the edge lane (the control plane when no compute node restarts a gateway). Every later host gets the follower gate, long enough to catch crash loops and immediate error spikes. scripts/ci/plan_edge_rollout.py checks these against the 30-minute budget (ADR-1650).

watch._comment: Post-deploy watch (docs/adr/20261020214632-automatic-unit-deploy-safety-rails.md): the SLO gate keeps running for `window` after a run's last activation, each rule held for its own for: (max hold = window). `max_blind_rounds` rounds without evidence (5 minutes at the interval) make it inconclusive. A host holds at most `max_unwatched` unit releases not yet watched clean, so release retention (3 previous releases) still holds its known-good release.

_migrations_comment: Goose migrations (*.sql directly in migrations_dir). When every one added since base is lane-eligible (declared -- migration-compat: expand, no contract change; docs/adr/20261018084150-unit-lane-expand-migrations.md), they are the data step the control-plane lane applies before restarting anything. Otherwise they block like any other path under blocking_paths.migrations.
_host_config_comment: Host configuration (docs/adr/20261018133100-host-configuration-lane.md). A deploy/ path a control-plane host role reads (scripts/ci/host_roles.py: the role's files and every path it names) no longer blocks the control-plane lane, which converges the roles whose content hash changed before it restarts anything (cd-controlplane.yml converge-host-config). A path a compute host role reads waits for the full release and holds the edge lane (compute_deploy) while that lane restarts a gateway on a compute host. release_units are the files cd-controlplane's bundle installs through deployctl at activation (systemd/, optional-systemd/, tmpfiles.d/): a unit release reuses the base's copies, so a change to one still needs a full release. stateful_services are services the lane never restarts: a role that can restart or stop one (a task, or a notified handler of any role, scripts/ci/host_roles.py restart_roles) blocks both lanes when its content changes (stateful_restart), the planner never selects it on its own, and in lane mode the roles refuse a restart (faas_stateful_restart_allowed).
_deploy_classes_comment: Every deploy/ path has exactly one class (docs/adr/20261027151755-unit-lane-deploy-path-classes.md; scripts/ci/affected_units.py deploy_class), first match wins: a release unit (host_config.release_units, blocking); a path a host role reads (host_config on the control plane, compute_deploy on compute); then the first class below with a pattern that names it. A pattern is a directory (trailing /), an exact path, or a glob (* inside one segment, **/ across segments). inert: nothing a host runs reads it at activation, so it maps to no flag: documentation, tests, samples (*.example, which roles install only as /etc/faas/*.example for operators to copy), the legacy unit tree deployctl generate writes for dev VMs (deploy/systemd/), the grafana role's dashboard mirror (deploy/grafana/, make grafana-mirror-check) and Cloudflare workers, which deploy through their own workflows. compute_only: playbooks only compute hosts run; pending for the control-plane lane, they hold the edge lane while it restarts a gateway on a compute host (compute_deploy). blocking: read by a full release or an operator path the lanes cannot vouch for, so a change waits for the next full tag (deploy). A path none of these names blocks, and scripts/ci/affected_units_test.py fails until it is classified. Whatever its class, a path no host role reads whose change since base only touches blank and # comment lines maps to no flag.
